linux_guest.native_deny_store: Installed selected Whiskey package, not a substitute store.
linux_guest.boot_ordering: The guest inherits Wants/Requires/After from the selected Forge egress unit, delays network readiness, and starts the real unit/consumer dependency chain.
linux_guest.native_state: Existing synthetic application SQLite rows survive the change to a preallocated UID while DynamicUser directory management and ID mapping remain enabled.
linux_guest.ingress: Actual Caddy and kernel UID filtering: backend refused to non-Caddy callers; loopback GET /metrics permits; other routes, methods and non-loopback connections refuse.
linux_guest.egress: Actual kernel IPv4 destination/port rules permit declared addresses, refuse another listening address, preserve unrelated UIDs, retire old DNS bindings and retain the prior complete boundary on failed resolution.
linux_guest.cleanup: The test driver terminated its exact guest QEMU process.

preserved_failed_attempt.failure: Disabling DynamicUser migrated the private StateDirectory pathname but left the existing ID-mapped SQLite data inaccessible.
preserved_failed_attempt.correction: Retain DynamicUser=yes with the explicitly preallocated NSS UID/GID, preserve the existing directory layout, and verify native deny access inside the service namespace.

review.resolved_finding: Initial DNS-dependent egress lacked network-online ordering, which could strand the consumer after a dependency-start failure.
review.correction: Explicit Wants/After network-online.target and an executed delayed-network dependency-chain regression.

limits: This is host preparation, state-custody, ingress and egress evidence, not a new complete N03/N06 or all-adapter gate.
W01-W03 native credential, operation, deny, model and caller qualification remains separately source-bound in the application repositories.
The guest uses synthetic state and a non-actuating HTTP backend; it does not claim a live Whiskey database migration or paid model request.
DNS-derived IPv4 address/port enforcement is not hostname attestation or image-only provider isolation.
Ordinary Desktop /api/mcp access remains native-authorized; the /cc/mcp route requires a separate resolver-signed companion.
Preparation and activation remain owner-operated. No live keys, grants, signers, sessions or household services were mutated.
